response.justification: Broad, long-tenured engineer with genuine AI-native exposure (current Staff role building MCP code generators and agentic tooling) and real high-throughput experience at Sociomantic/Dunnhumby (micro-services handling millions of HTTP requests/sec, low-latency async work). TypeScript is clearly at or above working level, and the craftsmanship signals — TDD, trunk-based development, CI/CD, open-source test tooling, teaching workshops — are strong. However, Python is absent from the skills list and every role description, which is a direct miss on a must-have. The distributed-systems depth is concentrated in a role that ended in 2020, and more recent work reads as full-stack product and platform engineering rather than architecture at scale. The resume also shows little evidence of cross-functional stakeholder management, technical strategy ownership, or on-call/incident response. Worth a screening call to probe Python depth and recent distributed-systems ownership, but not an obvious yes.
strengths: Hands-on AI-agent infrastructure and MCP tooling work; agentic development is already baseline for him
Proven high-throughput, low-latency micro-services experience (millions of requests/sec)
Deep engineering craftsmanship: TDD, CI/CD, open-source test frameworks, founder of an event-driven Kubernetes-deployed platform
concerns: Python not mentioned anywhere despite being a must-have; stack is TypeScript/Node/DLang-centric
Distributed-systems depth is dated (2018–2020); recent roles skew full-stack product work
Little evidence of technical strategy at scale, cross-functional stakeholder management, or on-call/incident ownership
